title: Beyond the 956: Jorge Juan Montejo, beloved Argentine comedian “Paolo el Rockero,” dies at 68
excerpt: Jorge Juan Montejo, the Argentine comedian who became a television icon as “Paolo el Rockero” in the 1980s and 1990s, died November 11, 2026, in Tandil, Argentina. He was 68.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Jorge Juan Montejo, the Argentine comedian who became a television icon as “Paolo el Rockero,” has died at 68.

Montejo died Wednesday, November 11, 2026, at 9:16 p.m. at the Ramón Santamarina Hospital in Tandil, his hometown, after several days hospitalized with pneumonia, Infobae reported, citing municipal sources. Ciudad Magazine, Revista Gente and El Tribuno de Jujuy also reported his death.

Born January 16, 1958, in Tandil, Montejo created the character of Paolo el Rockero in 1986, after Daniel Ripoll, founder of the magazine Pelo, suggested he try performing. Paolo — a long-haired rocker with a headband and a colorful shoulder bag — debuted on Badía & Cía, the program hosted by Juan Alberto Badía, and became an icon of Argentine popular culture through the 1980s and 1990s.

Montejo carried the character through Videomatch and Peligro sin codificar, and into the popular Bañeros film series, winning over generations of viewers with his absurd humor and trembling voice.

His death had been falsely reported twice before, in 2004 and 2011, making Wednesday’s confirmed reports all the more painful for fans who had hoped the news was another hoax.

Rest in Peace, Jorge Juan Montejo.

Sources: Infobae; Ciudad Magazine; Revista Gente; El Tribuno de Jujuy.
